# Plot Posterior Predictive Densities Versus Observed Data

## Description

This function draws kernel-density curves for posterior-predictive samples and observed data using `ggplot2::geom_line()`. Each predictive sample’s density is plotted in light blue; the observed density is overlaid in black.

```r
plot_ppd(
  ppd,
  obs,
  xlab = "Outcome",
  ylab = "Density",
  title = "Posterior Predictive Distribution",
  xlim = NULL,
  obs_color = NULL,
  ppd_color = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

- `ppd`: A `matrix` containing posterior predictive samples (one column per sample).
- `obs`: A vector of observations, must have the same length as the number of columns in `ppd`.
- `xlab`: Character: x-axis label. Default `"Outcome"`.
- `ylab`: Character: y-axis label. Default `"Density"`.
- `title`: Character: plot title. Default `"Posterior Predictive Distribution"`.
- `xlim`: Numeric vector of length 2 giving the minimum and maximum x-axis values, e.g. `c(0, 25)`. If `NULL` (default) the limits are `c(0, quantile(observed, 0.95))`.
- `obs_color`: Color for the observed line density.
- `ppd_color`: Color for the posterior predictive distribution line density.

## Returns

A `ggplot2` plot object.

## Examples

```r
# Load example dataset
data(dengue_MS)
dengue_MS <- dengue_MS[dengue_MS$year %in% 2015:2016,]

# Declare formulas
formulas <- "dengue_cases ~ tmin + f(year, model='rw1')"

# Tranform formulas into a 'GHRformulas' object
ghr_formula <- as_GHRformulas(formulas)

# Fit multiple models
results <- fit_models(
  formulas = ghr_formula,
  data = dengue_MS,
  family = "nbinomial",
  name = "model",
  offset_var = "pop100000",
  nthreads = 2,
  control_compute = list(config = TRUE),
  keep_ppd = TRUE,
  ppd_samples = 50
)

# Plot densities of the posterior predictive distribution and observed cases.
plot_ppd(results$ppd[[1]], obs = dengue_MS$dengue_cases)
```
